decisions.rationale: Approvals bind to concrete target identity and Environment signal alone cannot grant destructive authority share the permissions_security_privacy subsystem and relevant vocabulary, but the strict merge test fails. Their endpoint summaries, source authorities, lifecycle stages, user outcomes, state boundaries, and failure/recovery promises remain independently testable, so they are preserved as distinct subsystem features.
decisions.authority_lifecycle_outcome_state_failur: Authority: OPF::A005OM-0012::PF-0201 belongs to A005OM-0012/Plans/Decision_Policy.md, whereas OPF::A005OM-0013::PF-0033 belongs to A005OM-0013/Plans/FileSafe.md. Lifecycle and outcome: "Approvals bind to concrete target identity" governs DP-058 requires target-bound approval and preflight identity, preserves domain-specific target fields before mutation, and expressly rejects action-name-only binding for multi-repository projects., while "Environment signal alone cannot grant destructive authority" governs F2-028 requires a trustworthy baseline and a current authenticated override grant; it explicitly treats PUPPET_MASTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE as a request signal, not authority.. State boundary and failure semantics differ as shown by their separate gaps: A=No gap in this observation; preserve the explicit contract and its stated boundary.; B=Explicit non-gap or affirmative contract: F2-028 requires a trustworthy baseline and a current authenticated override grant; it explicitly treats PUPPET_MASTER_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE as a request signal, not authority.. Shared domain, adjacency, common controls, or umbrella/member structure do not satisfy full equivalence.
